purpose: Define what each Rust crate is allowed to be in the CYNIC organism so runtime, protocol, mobile, inference, node and adapter code do not fragment into competing authorities.

crate_classes.meaning: Central nervous-system process owning durable coordination, task memory, observations, health and read-back APIs.
Agent-facing portable tool projection over kernel and organism capabilities.
Per-machine local sensor, supervisor and bounded actuator.
Structured proof-of-history, lineage and semantic memory tooling.
Evaluation, judge and Dog inference runtime separated from the kernel when inference becomes a process.
Host or device sensor that emits observations into the organism.
Product or application domain library consumed by apps or protocols, not organism infrastructure.
Blockchain program crate with chain-specific execution constraints.
Visible Rust crate not yet accepted as a canonical workspace/runtime surface.

crate_families.meaning: Shared organism bus, memory, coordination, surfaces and proof read-back.
Per-machine body runtime: host supervision, local sensing, bounded actuation and runtime artifact proof.
Physical, cognitive, device or environmental input surfaces that emit observations.
Inference, evaluation, verdicts, Dogs and gates.
Application or product domain libraries that may live in the repo but are not organism infrastructure.
On-chain or external protocol programs whose execution authority lives outside the off-chain organism.
Visible crates whose role, naming or workspace placement is unresolved.

family_rules: A crate family is organic placement, not a build target.
A crate class is technical responsibility, not product identity.
A crate may have one primary family only; cross-family coupling must be declared through dependencies or runtime_artifacts.
If a name suggests a different family than the declared family, record naming_debt before promotion.
Do not create a new Rust crate while an existing crate can absorb the responsibility without crossing its class boundary.

workspace_policy.member_rule: A crate in Cargo.toml workspace.members must have a declared crate role here before it can be treated as canonical organism runtime.
workspace_policy.visible_non_member_rule: A crate directory with Cargo.toml that is not in workspace.members is transitional until this contract classifies it and the repo topology contract accepts or quarantines it.
workspace_policy.onchain_rule: On-chain program crates may live in the workspace for build ergonomics, but they do not become organism runtime services.

crate_scarcity_policy.rule: New crates are exceptional. Prefer adding a bounded module to an existing crate family, then expose it through Kernel or MCP only after the contract is stable.
crate_scarcity_policy.python_vital_function_rule: A Python vital-function migration target must be a declared crate here and must expose python_absorption_authority describing what it is allowed to absorb.

default_absorption_targets.need: Solana/Pump/PumpSwap parsing, discriminators, Token-2022 account classification and deterministic token analysis
default_absorption_targets.reason: This is judgment and mechanism analysis, not a separate runtime authority.

default_absorption_targets.need: Kernel storage, observation read-back, task memory or library query APIs
default_absorption_targets.reason: Kernel owns durable memory and bus semantics.

default_absorption_targets.need: Agent-facing tool schema or command exposure
default_absorption_targets.reason: MCP owns portable agent tool projection.

default_absorption_targets.need: Per-machine supervision, local probes or host actuation

exception_requires: proof that no existing crate family can absorb the module
declared class and family in this contract
tests proving the new crate has a stable boundary

crate_naming_policy.rule: Crate names must describe stable organism function, runtime layer, or product domain; they must not encode a temporary persona, brand metaphor, or implementation fad as infrastructure authority.
discouraged_patterns: agent framework names for deterministic controllers
product names for organism-wide runtime services

promotion_requirements: A visible non-member crate must be either added to workspace.members with a canonical class or explicitly quarantined.
A crate-shaped directory without Cargo.toml must be deleted, moved out of crates, or explicitly listed as quarantine in this contract.
A runtime crate must have a matching runtime_artifacts entry before it is deployed as a release binary.
A crate may implement a policy only when the corresponding docs/foundation policy and axiom contract already define it.
Application and on-chain crates must not be used to justify organism runtime coupling.
